messages:
maria_support: Hey team — opening an escalation for AcmeRetail. They've hit repeated failures on the embeddings endpoint since ~09:40 UTC. Customer says some requests return "dimension mismatch" errors and others return correct vectors, and overall latency is spiking. They reported region=eu-west in their dashboard but are supposed to be in us-west. Can someone triage? :eyes:

eli_cs: Copying Acme POC (cc: @acme_infra). They're seeing intermittent 400s with this body: "error: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024". They send batches of mixed document sets — unsure if client changed model. Customer also says billing shows requests routed to eu-west for a few mins then to us-west.

liam_sre: I'm pulling traces. I see a routing fallback event around 09:42:17 where traffic for acme-customer-id spilled into eu-west due to us-west GPU pool briefly reporting 0 available instances during a scale event. Autoscaler log: "scale_down_delay misconfigured -> temporary underprovisioning". That explains region mismatch. If they hit a different model variant in eu-west (smaller quantized model) dims could be different.

sophie_platform: Important note: our embed-model-family has two variants with different output dims for historical reasons. redwood-embed-small-v1 -> 1024, redwood-embed-large-v1 -> 1536. If routing flips models mid-batch, client will observe dimension mismatch. We should ensure routing preserves model_id per-request or reject mixed-model batches.

raj_engineer: Repro steps I ran:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acmeprod" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-v1","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```
On us-west I get 1536 vectors fine. Force region header to eu-west (for testing):
```
-H "X-Region: eu-west"
```
I then got 1024 vectors. Error reproduces if client batches items that were encoded by two different model variants and then tries to unpack with a fixed dims of 1536.

maria_support: Customer code snippet (they sent):
```
# python
inputs = [doc.text for doc in docs]
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-embed-large-v1", input=inputs, batch_size=128)
# they assume model always returns 1536
vectors = [r['embedding'] for r in resp['data']]
```
They use default endpoint URL with no explicit region param.

eli_cs: Acme's billing + graph shows ~09:42-09:45 window where ~30% of embedding ops were serviced by eu-west. They have a steady qps that triggered autoscale burst. Looks like our router allowed cross-region spillover when local capacity < threshold.

liam_sre: Two immediate pain points: (1) cross-region fallback can route to a different model variant when the configured model id maps to different builds across regions; (2) cold starts / fast scale-up created a small time window where instances didn't advertise full model registry. Both can produce dimension mismatches and latency spikes. Measured metrics: p50 ~ 230ms -> p95 ~ 1.2s during the event; error rate 4.6% for that 3-minute window.

sophie_platform: Short-term mitigations we can push right now:
- force-fail cross-region routing for model families with non-uniform dims (safe-mode) — return 503 instead of routing.
- add soft validation that checks returned embedding length and rejects batch with clear error early.
- add a warning in console for customers using redwood-embed-large-v1 that region mapping could differ during spillover.

raj_engineer: I can patch the router to add a model-dimension check hook: when selecting a replica, verify replica.model_config.output_dim == expected_dim and otherwise skip replica. That will reduce spillover but could increase 503s under pressure. Deploy can be scoped to production gradually.

elaine_cs: Customer asks for a hotfix now — they need their service stable. Can we suggest client-side changes that are low-friction?

liam_sre: Short-term client guidance to give Acme:
1) Pin model id explicitly to exact variant (e.g., redwood-embed-large-v1@2025-11-02) to avoid region mapping ambiguity.
2) Check embedding vector length and fail fast with a clear metric and alert if wrong dims are returned.
3) Reduce batch_size temporarily (64->32) to reduce chance of mixing model outputs if routing switches mid-batch.
4) Use region-specific endpoint (e.g., us-west.api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings) or set header X-Preferred-Region: us-west to prefer local pool.

maria_support: I pushed those guidance steps to the customer. They can accept client changes; they prefer server-side fix though. They've also provided us their request_ids for failures: req_98765, req_98786, req_98802.

liam_sre: I traced req_98786: router decision log:
```
[09:42:23] router: choose pool us-west (downscale event) -> fallback policy: spillover -> selected replica eu-west-3a -> model_variant redwood-embed-small-v1
```
And corresponding backend log:
```
[09:42:23] embed-service[eu-west-3a]: loaded model redwood-embed-small-v1 (output_dim=1024)
[09:42:24] infer: batch_size=120 latency=780ms
```
Client expected 1536 -> got 1024 -> app failed with dimension mismatch on their side.

sophie_platform: I've flagged cross-region model parity as a priority. We should maintain a region mapping table so the same model id resolves to parity models only; otherwise require explicit variant name. Also need to re-evaluate spillover policy for latency-sensitive endpoints like embeddings.

raj_engineer: Proposed short deployment plan:
- hotfix router check (only route to replica if output_dim matches expected) -> can roll within 30m to reduce mismatches. (risk: increased 503 under high load)
- telemetry: emit metric 'embedding_dim_mismatch_count' and create dashboard + alert
- longer-term: unify model artifact names across regions or return deterministic model-not-available rather than fall back to different variant

eli_cs: Customer accepted client pins for now and will lower batch_size. They've requested we ETA hotfix and a postmortem. They also want a credit for failed requests in that 3-minute window.

maria_support: Finance + billing: can we pre-approve a small credit for 3-minute spike? They lost production reliability during that window.

finance: I'll approve a discretionary credit up to $1k for operational impact. We'll calculate actual token usage later.

liam_sre: Quick follow-ups I did: I pushed a temporary router rule to prefer same-region replicas strictly for embeddings for Acme's tenant id. That should stop any further cross-region routing for them immediately. Monitoring shows no more 400s for the tenant in the last 12m.

sophie_platform: I'll start the patch for the model-dimension check and telemetry. Raj, can you prepare the PR for router behavior and include a feature flag? We'll gate roll by canary to 10% of traffic.

raj_engineer: On it — PR branch: feat/router-embed-dim-check. Patch includes:
```
if replica.output_dim != model_registry[model_id].expected_dim:
    skip_replica()
```
Feature flag: router.embed_dim_validation (default off)

elaine_cs: Customer asked for a plain-language explanation for their execs. Draft I proposed:
"Between 09:42–09:45 UTC, some of your embedding requests were routed to a different data center where a smaller embedding model was temporarily used by our fallback policy. That model produces shorter vectors (1024 vs 1536) which caused your service to reject the responses. We've applied a temporary rule to keep your traffic in your preferred region and are rolling a fix to prevent routing to mismatched models in the future. We will follow up with a postmortem and a small credit for impacted requests." :white_check_mark:

maria_support: Acme responded: "Thanks, the temporary rule fixed it. We'll implement client pins as well. Please send postmortem and let us know when fix is live." They also asked whether future spillover could be to a model with the same dimension — want guarantees.

sophie_platform: We'll promise to ensure model-dimension parity as a product goal for embeddings; will align with model ops to sync artifacts across regions. I'll own follow-up and timeline.

liam_sre: Action items summary:
- raj: deploy router dim-check behind flag (PR + canary) — ETA 3h
- sophie: model parity roadmap + console warning — ETA EOW
- maria/elaine: customer comms + credit — in progress
- finance: finalize credit after token accounting
- monitoring: create embed_dim_mismatch_count metric + dashboard — ETA 1h

maria_support: Thanks all. Marking this thread resolved once PR is in and customer gets the postmortem. :pray:
